hints: Remember that complete combustion always makes the same two products, so start by balancing carbon and hydrogen first.
With $n$ carbons in $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$, you must make $n$ molecules of $\text{CO}_2$, and with $2n$ hydrogens you must make $n$ molecules of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Now count all the oxygen atoms needed on the right side and work out how many $\text{O}_2$ molecules that corresponds to on the left.
walkthrough:
**Write the products for complete combustion**

Complete combustion of any hydrocarbon gives only carbon dioxide and water. So start with an unbalanced skeleton:
$$\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Balance carbon and hydrogen first**

There are $n$ C atoms on the left, so we need $n$ $\text{CO}_2$ on the right. There are $2n$ H atoms on the left, so we need $n$ $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ on the right (since each water has 2 H):
$$\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow n\text{CO}_2 + n\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Balance oxygen last**

Now count O atoms on the right. From $n\text{CO}_2$ we have $2n$ O, and from $n\text{H}_2\text{O}$ we have $n$ O. Total is $3n$ O atoms.
$$\text{O atoms needed} = 2n + n = 3n$$
Since each $\text{O}_2$ provides 2 O atoms, moles of $\text{O}_2 = \frac{3n}{2}$:
$$\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n} + \frac{3}{2}n\text{O}_2 \rightarrow n\text{CO}_2 + n\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: The oxygen is correct but the water is wrong. $2n\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $4n$ hydrogen atoms, but the alkene only provides $2n$ hydrogens. This doubles the hydrogen count.
options.B: This balances perfectly. Carbon: $n$ on both sides. Hydrogen: $2n$ on both sides ($n \times 2$ in water). Oxygen: $3n$ atoms on both sides ($\frac{3}{2}n \times 2$ on left, $2n + n$ on right).
options.C: The carbon and water are correct ($n\text{CO}_2 + n\text{H}_2\text{O}$), but $2n\text{O}_2$ gives $4n$ oxygen atoms while only $3n$ are needed. Students who guess the oxygen coefficient often pick this.
options.D: Both oxygen and water are wrong. $2n\text{H}_2\text{O}$ gives too much hydrogen ($4n$ H instead of $2n$ H), and $2n\text{O}_2$ gives too much oxygen. Nothing balances except carbon.
